chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The supplication is answered in four places/times: in the Witr prayer, and after the Fajr prayer, and after the Dhuhr prayer, and after the Maghrib prayer."
ai.seo_question: What are the four specific times when du'a is answered according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies four specific moments—during Witr and after Fajr, Dhuhr, and Maghrib—as times when supplications are particularly likely to be answered, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual potency of post-obligatory prayer intervals. This tradition underscores the concept of 'Qabul al-Da'wah' (acceptance of prayer) linked to the transition between divine commands and human devotion, a theme deeply rooted in the daily rhythm of worship.
